chunks: Sulaiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari narrated from Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Nakha'i, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man from among the Muslims whom a thief had entrusted with dirhams or goods, while the thief is a Muslim. Should he return it to him?

He عليه السلام said: “He should not return it to him. If he is able to return it to its owner, he should do so. Otherwise, it remains in his possession with the status of lost property that he comes upon, so he should announce it for one year. If he finds its owner, [he returns it to him]; otherwise, he should give it in charity. If its owner comes after that, he is given the choice between the reward and the compensation. If he chooses the reward, then the reward is his; and if he chooses compensation, he compensates him for it, and the reward belongs to him.”

key_terms.اللُّصُوصِ: thieves; those who unlawfully took the property
key_terms.اللُّقَطَةِ: lost property that is found and must be publicly announced
key_terms.الْغُرْمِ: financial liability or repayment due to the owner
key_terms.تَصَدَّقَ: he gives it in charity on behalf of the owner
key_terms.دَرَاهِمَ: dirhams; coined money entrusted by the thief
key_terms.مَتَاعًا: goods or belongings of material value

ai.seo_question: What should be done with property deposited by a thief if the rightful owner is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about property entrusted by a thief: it must not be returned to the thief, but instead should be restored to its rightful owner if possible. If the owner is unknown, it is treated as lost property, announced for a year, then given in charity, while preserving the owner's later right either to the reward or to repayment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4065 - Sulaiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari narrated from Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Nakha'i, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a Muslim man who was entrusted with dirhams or goods by a thief, and the thief is also a Muslim. Should he return them to him?

Imam (as) said: "He should not return them to him. If he is able to return them to their rightful owner, he should do so. Otherwise, he should treat them as lost property (luqata), announcing them for one year.
If the rightful owner is found, he should return them to him. Otherwise, he should give them in charity.
If the owner later comes forward, he should be given the choice between accepting the reward for the charity or demanding repayment.
If he chooses the reward, it is his. If he chooses repayment, the person must compensate him, and the reward for the charity remains with the one who gave it."
